summary: Full backend + frontend testing of Scheduled Scans and Notifications feature. All 6 backend API tests pass (limits/info, list, full CRUD lifecycle including toggle pause/resume, update interval, duplicate/limit rejection, delete-then-404, notifications list + unread-count + mark-all-read, and auth-required for both). Frontend Playwright test covers: login, nav Scheduled link with clock icon between Analytics and Pricing, NotificationBell visible with 'No notifications yet' empty state, /scheduled-scans page loads with '0/1 scheduled scan used' free-user limit display, create modal opens, creates scan for weekly interval, list shows URL + 'Weekly' interval text, upgrade prompt appears once limit reached, pause toggles to Paused badge, resume works, delete removes the scan. No console/page errors detected.

minor.issue: Duplicate-URL check (400) is unreachable for Free plan because the limit check (403) short-circuits first. Not a bug but consider re-ordering checks so users on their limit trying to re-add the SAME URL get a more actionable message.

critical_code_review_comments: scheduled.py: order of duplicate vs limit check — Free user re-adding same URL sees 'limit reached' instead of 'already exists'. Consider checking duplicate first.

scheduled.py: get_scheduled_scan_limits_info returns current_user.plan as an enum (UserPlan.free). FastAPI serializes it to 'free' via use_enum_values in the model config; verified via live response ('plan': 'free'). Safe as-is.
NotificationBell: polls every 30s — fine for MVP but consider WebSocket/SSE for real-time behavior.

ScheduledScansPage.formatNextRun uses Math.ceil on delta which produces 'In 8 days' immediately after creating a 7-day scan (because a few ms are added). Minor UX polish opportunity — expected 'In 7 days'.
handleToggle / handleDelete use alert() and window.confirm() rather than styled UI — inconsistent with the rest of the app which uses inline error banners.
No pagination on GET /notifications and /scheduled-scans (both cap at 100). Fine now, revisit at scale.
seed_data_creation: During API + UI testing, temporarily created scheduled scans for https://test-lifecycle.example.com and https://frontend-test.example.com; both were deleted at end of tests. Free user ends with 0/1 scheduled scans used (previously stated pre-existing example.com scan was deleted as part of clean-slate step in lifecycle test).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Scheduled scans + notifications feature verified end-to-end. verifytest@example.com currently has 0 scheduled scans (cleaned up). Notification collection is empty for this user. Backend scheduler runs every 60s; to observe a notification flowing E2E you can create a scheduled scan with interval_days=1 and wait ~1 min after next_run (though next_run is now+interval so first fire is 1 day out — not practical without DB manipulation).
